en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on the Circular Gaze 8.
The Second Training Rule on the Cast-Down Eyes.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas looking here and there... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I will sit in inhabited areas with eyes cast down.
One should sit in inhabited areas with eyes cast down, looking only a plough's length ahead."
If one, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area looking here and there, it is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who lacks mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
